title: Campaign: connectomes, from wiring to activity and behaviour
abstract: Subcampaign of 'what do connectomes reveal about how nervous systems are built?'. Scope: Tests of whether wiring predicts measured activity, response properties or behaviour. 10 papers. Status: mixed. Wiring matched receptor expression (histamine receptors best); a flyvis model and FlyWire counts correlate (r 0.71); passive cable models match receptive fields of some large visual types; but predicted transmitter signs did not improve ON/OFF polarity prediction, a whole-brain model gave different responses for left and right inputs, and C. elegans perturbation predictions only partly repeat across datasets. Diffusion tractography adds little to the prediction of individual functional connectivity (own structural connectivity explains about 0.15% of reliable individual variance).
